name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 6, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:04
p.m., on July 6, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 1, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations—The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are

City Council Minutes  1  July 6, 2009
   the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel—Initiation of Litigation. Pursuant to Subdivision
  (c) of Government Code Section 54956.9. Two (2) Cases Under Consideration.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
  Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, the Council
  received a report and gave direction to their negotiator. For item CS2, there were no
  decisions made and there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winner

  Michelle Clark from Waste Management presented the Recycling Award to Les and Irena
  Cromwell.

P2.  Proclaim July 2009 as Parks and Recreation Month

  Mayor Ury presented the Proclamation to Community Services Commission Chairman,
  Brian Skalsky.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Bruce G. Hunt, M.V.: recognized members of the Marine Adoption Committee and
  thanked the City and its residents for supporting the Headquarters Battalion of the First
  Marine Division and their families.

  Major Andrew Munro: introduced Sergeant Major Fascetti and thanked the Council, the
  City of Mission Viejo, and the Marine Adoption Committee for tireless efforts in
  supporting the First Headquarters Battalion Marines. Major Munro presented Bruce Hunt
  with a U.S. flag which was flown over Camp Al Taqaddum in Iraq, as a token of their
  thanks and as a tribute to the support received from the Adoption Committee.

  The following spoke in support of cultural and public arts and asked the City to continue

City Council Minutes  2  July 6, 2009
   supporting these programs: Aileen May, Dana Point; Jennifer Koons, M.V.; Pat Wayne,
  M.V.; Casey Hanenkrat, M.V. and Buff Webster, M.V.

  The following presented a written in support of public art in the City of Mission Viejo:
  Lynda Zimmer, M.V.

  Les Sykes, M.V.: asked Council Member Schlicht to apologize to the Community
  Services Commission for comments she made at the last meeting regarding the
  qualifications of Commission Members in reviewing the recent Recreation Centers
  Master Plan.

  Patricia Powers, M.V.: inquired about a comment made at the recent budget workshop
  regarding privatization of the library. Ms. Powers asked why dog parks and recreation
  centers take priority over the education of our children.

  Beth Mconaughy, incoming President of the Mission Viejo Friends of the Library, M.V.:
  outlined the efforts of the Friends of the Library and the income they contribute towards
  the purchase of books and library programs. She stated that the Mission Viejo Library is
  a grand resource for the community and she is proud to be part of the Friends of the
  Library.

  Gloria Heer, M.V.: expressed her appreciation to the City Council, the Mission Viejo
  Activities Committee, and city staff who made it possible to enjoy such a safe and fun 4th
  of July celebration.

  F.K. (Joe) Holtzman, M.V.: stated that the City should be considering an audit of
  Southern California Edison as a source of revenue. He stated that Edison owes the City
  money which could go a long way towards support of the library and the City’s arts
  programs.

  Trina Robertson, M.V.: expressed support for the Kids Factory program and stated that
  she is comforted knowing that her kids are in a safe place to bridge the gap between the
  end of school and the time she is able to pick them up after work. She asked the Council
  to consider continuing to fund the Kids Factory in Mission Viejo.

  Christine Saracino, M.V.: announced that she and her neighbors are still waiting for a
  copy of the signed agreement between the City and the owner of 26992 La Paja for the
  timeline of the construction project at that address.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she was interested in trying to find a way to save the
  Kids Factory Program and therefore she suggested consolidating some of the sites. She
  further discussed her comment about privatizing the library as a way to save money.
  Council Member Schlicht stated that she stands firm in the opinion that the Planning
  Commission would have done a better job with the Tennis Centers Master Plan.

City Council Minutes  3  July 6, 2009
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

A motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
approve the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the City Council Minutes for the Regular meeting of June 15, 2009, as
  presented; and (2) approved the City Council Minutes for the Budget Workshop of June
  22, 2009, as presented.

3.  Check Register dated June 5, 2009, in the amount of $740,471.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated June 12, 2009, in the amount of $570,949.67

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Adoption of the 2009-11 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Agency

  Approved CDA Resolution 09-02 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Agency for 2009-11 and appropriating funds for FY 2009-10 only.

7.  Adoption of FY 2009-10 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development

City Council Minutes  4  July 6, 2009
   Financing Authority

  Approved CDFA Resolution 09-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2009-10 Fiscal Year.

8.  Acceptable Condition Levels for the City’s Street Network

  Established the range of acceptable average condition levels for all classifications of road
  types within the City's street network at either "Very Good" or "Excellent," as defined by
  the Pavement Condition Index (PCI), for fiscal years 2009-10 and 2010-11.

10.  Park, Right-of-Way, and Facility Electrical, Lighting Maintenance Repair and
  Replacement

  (1) Awarded the contract for the subject services to C & D Electric, Inc. for the period of
  July 1, 2009, to June 30, 2011, in the amount of $531,460.00; and (2) authorized issuance
  of a purchase order to C & D Electric, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2009, to June 30,
  2010, in an amount not to exceed $265,730.00.

14.  2009-2011 School Crossing Guard Services

  (1) Awarded the contract in the amount of $735,292 to All City Management Services,
  Inc., for school crossing guard services for the period July 1, 2009, to June 30, 2011; and
  (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to All City Management Services, Inc., in an
  amount not to exceed $367,646 for the period July 1, 2009, to June 30, 2010.

17.  2009 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the 2009 Residential Resurfacing--Slurry Seal Project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

18.  Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on
  Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program 2009 - Phase
  1

  Mayor Ury opened the public hearing at 7:01 p.m.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  5  July 6, 2009
   There were no requests from the public to speak on this item, therefore Mayor Ury closed
  the public hearing at 7:02 p.m.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to direct the Director of Public Services to proceed and perform removal of weeds in
  accordance with Section 39569 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  Check Register dated June 19, 2009, in the amount of $1,827,150.87

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about an expenditure listed as item number 5-20 on
  page 20 of the report for True North Research to conduct a building services customer
  survey.

  City Manager Wilberg stated that direction was given by the City Council, as part of the
  City Manager review a year ago, to conduct a customer satisfaction survey for the City's
  building counter. Mr. Wilberg announced that the survey has recently been completed
  and the results will be presented to the City Council in the near future.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Barcelona Walls - Trabuco Road at Marguerite Parkway and Jeronimo Road at
  Marguerite Parkway

City Council Minutes  6  July 6, 2009
   Director of Community Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: expressed concern with the amount the City paid for Barcelona
  walls at Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway and Jeronimo Road and Marguerite
  Parkway.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to (1) authorize the City Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange
  and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days,
  respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with or by the City; and (2) authorize the payment of the final
  retention of $9,705.00 thirty-five days after the date of recordation of the Notice of
  Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

11.  Proposed Lease Agreement Submitted by Royal Street Communications in
  Conjunction with Proposal to Construct a Wireless Telecommunications Facility at
  Beebe Park, 24190 Olympiad Road, on Property Owned by the City of Mission
  Viejo

  Council Member Schlicht outlined concerns that were brought up by the Planning and
  Transportation Commissioners and stated that she was disturbed with the quality of the
  maps that were given to the Planning Commissioners.

  A motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley,
  to approve and authorize the City Manager to Execute the Lease.

  Council Member Schlicht made an amendment to the motion to direct the installation of
  EMF warning signs around the tot lot at Beebe park. The amendment died for lack of a
  second.

  On roll call, said original motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht

City Council Minutes  7  July 6, 2009
   ABSENT:  None

12.  Antique and Antique Art Show Sponsorship

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Frank Lieberman, M.V.: thanked the City for supporting his Fun With Chalk event over
  the years and requested the City’s support for the Antique and Antique Art Show. He
  stated that he now proposes to conduct a one-day show on March 13, 2010, which would
  involve use of the Community Center facilities for 2½ days rather than the originally
  proposed three-day show, requiring use of the facilities for five days. Dr. Lieberman
  stated that he would use volunteers as much as possible to minimize the need for City
  staff and he announced that he is interested in the possibility of merging Fun With Chalk
  with Artes de la Vida in May of 2010 for one great event.

  A motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1) move
  forward with the newly proposed one-day event and allow the Creative Arts Productions
  Foundation (CAP) to use the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center
  beginning at 3:00 p.m. on Friday, March 12th, all day Saturday, March 13, 2010, for the
  Antique Show, and Sunday, March 14, 2010, for clean-up; and (2) direct City Staff to
  work with the Creative Arts Productions Foundation Board to do everything in their
  power to ensure that the Fun with Chalk event occurs in 2010, in addition to this Antique
  Show.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  Professional Services Agreement for State Legislative Advocacy Services

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she doesn't understand why the City needs two
  lobbyists. We obtain information from the League of California Cities and she doesn't
  agree with spending $62,000 a year for help in writing grant applications.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  MacLean, Approve a Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs for
  State legislative advocacy services in an amount not to exceed $62,000 for the period of
  July 1, 2009 to June 30, 2010.

City Council Minutes  8  July 6, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

15.  Montanoso Drive Traffic Calming Improvements (CIP 779)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the completion of the Montanoso Drive Traffic
  Calming Improvements: Bob Grovich, M.V.; Bert Van Dyk, M.V.; and Jim Grissom,
  M.V.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean,
  to approve the recommended actions for the completion of the Montanoso Drive Traffic
  Calming Improvements per Exhibit A of the Agenda report.

  A motion was made by Council Member Schlicht to table this item to allow for a formal
  staff presentation on the proposed project. The motion died for lack of a second.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

16.  American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 Street Improvement Project
  (CIPs 202/837)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the report.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she would like the Council to take a stance and
  reject all stimulus monies because it is a tax burden for future generations.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean,
  to approve the bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  9  July 6, 2009
   AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

19.  Integrated Solid Waste Management Services Ad Hoc Committee

  Mayor Ury appointed himself and Mayor Pro Tem MacLean to serve on an Integrated
  Solid Waste Management Services Ad Hoc Committee.

20.  Oso Creek Trail Project

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Gloria Heer, M.V.: expressed her support for the project and stated that the kiosks will be
  a worthwhile addition and will encourage increased use of the Oso Creek Trail.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1)
  approve the Community Services Commission’s recommendation regarding the Oso
  Creek Trail Connection and Enhancement Project for signage on the trail and kiosks at
  the entrance of the trails; and (2) award a contract to 4C Development (A09-26) in an
  amount not to exceed $164,266.00 for the installation of the comprehensive Trail and
  Kiosk sign program (CIP 317).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

21.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:48 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:59
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  10  July 6, 2009
 22.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA. There is a meeting scheduled on Thursday, July 9, 2009, so he
  will have a report at the next City Council Meeting.

23.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA and he will have a report at the next City Council Meeting.

24.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

25.  2009-11 Proposed Budget - Additional Information

  City Manager Wilberg outlined the information and analysis that is presented in the
  agenda report as follow-up to questions posed by the City Council at the last meeting.

  The City Council Members reviewed the responses to the information requests and
  further discussed areas of interest or concern regarding the Proposed 2009-11 budget,
  including the service impact of cuts, one-time non-essential costs, options if gas tax funds
  were taken by the State, and estimates for special election costs. The Council asked
  questions and directed staff to return at the July 20, 2009, meeting with information on:
  (1) changes to the Library budget; (2) proposed cutbacks in City contributions for
  ceremonial wreaths and to various community organizations; (3) possible restoration of
  funding for the Marguerite slope renovation program; (4) possible restoration of funding
  for irrigation technical upgrades; and (5) Southern California Edison (SCE) franchise fee
  collections/audits.

  A motion was made by Council Member Schlicht to (1) eliminate the proposed 75%
  reduction for library materials and reinstate it into the budget; (2) reinstate the Library’s
  adult computer classes; and (3) reinstate the Youth Story Time programs. The motion
  died for lack of a second.

City Council Minutes  11  July 6, 2009
 City Attorney’s Report

  City Attorney Bill Curley stated that he is heartened to hear the Council's support for
  ethical conduct because that has a lot of bearing on many of the projects he is working
  on.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

26.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is not claiming mileage for reimbursement
  purposes.

Council Member Kelley

  Council Member Kelley announced that she really enjoyed the 4th of July Street Faire
  and she complimented the Mission Viejo Activities Committee, in particular
  Chairpersons Dave and Cathy Allen. She also thanked the entire Committee for their
  volunteer efforts and for always putting on a wonderful event. Council Member Kelley
  thanked Mayor Pro Tem MacLean for volunteering to do vendor check-in and for coming
  back later to spend the afternoon at the Faire. She further thanked Mayor Ury and
  Council Member Ledesma for attending and showing the City’s support for the event.
  Council Member Kelley also recognized Bruce Hunt, the Marine Adoption Committee,
  and the Marines from our adopted Headquarters Battalion for their work at the Faire.
  Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month
  of July is fairness.

Council Member Ledesma

  Council Member Ledesma shared his own thanks to the Mission Viejo Activities
  Committee for once again making the 4th of July Street Faire a great event and he
  thanked City staff and the Sheriff's Department for their coordination efforts and for
  making it all possible.

Council Member Schlicht

  Council Member Schlicht stated that this is the first year that she didn’t make it to the 4th
  of July Street Faire. Originally she was to be out of town but her plans changed and she

City Council Minutes  12  July 6, 2009
   returned home late that day. She ended up attending the Tea Party and stated that it was a
  great event with a lot of enthusiasm. She recognized that Tea Parties are well-received in
  these extraordinary economic times and she noted that there have been ten pages of
  foreclosure notices in the Saddleback Valley News and that unemployment is at an all
  time high. Council Member Schlicht stated that we don’t seem to be paying much
  attention to that and our character is only as strong as our behavior. She stated that there
  is angst against her for signing the recall petition but she feels that Mayor Pro Tem
  MacLean’s conduct towards Dr. Lieberman this evening is reason to make sure that that
  the recall is successful.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that he believes the Council needs to have dialogue and
  his questions to Dr. Lieberman were straight forward and pointed but at no time did he
  disrespect him. He further noted that he did not call Dr. Lieberman “wrong-headed,
  disingenuous, empty-headed or ignorant” yet he has heard those words from Council
  Member Schlicht in the past and he feels she should practice what she preaches. Mayor
  Pro Tem MacLean noted that he does respect and appreciate Dr. Lieberman and he
  actually prefaced his comments and questions that way this evening. He also observed
  that Dr. Lieberman got defensive and outlined the hours he volunteers to the City, and
  while the City appreciates that, there are hundreds of people who volunteer their time
  selflessly, for example the Senior Community Activity Team (SCAT), the Heritage
  Committee, the Youth Activities Committee, the Community of Character Committee,
  the Friends of the Library, and the Dedicated Animal Welfare Group (DAWG). Mayor
  Pro Tem MacLean stated that people volunteer because they love this community without
  the need to brag about the time they serve and he too volunteers without talking about it
  because he wants to do what is right. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean thanked the Mission
  Viejo Activities Committee and stated that he had a great time at the Street Faire and he
  especially enjoyed the dunk booth. He looks forward to many more Activities
  Committee events and to being a part of that organization.

Mayor Ury

  Mayor Ury reiterated what fun the 4th of July Street Faire was. He participated in the
  dunk tank and noted that next year, the water should be changed after six people have
  been in the tank. He joked that the kids did a better job of hitting the target and dunking
  him this year than the adults did. Mayor Ury offered his congratulations to the Mission
  Viejo Activities Committee who always do a fantastic job.

ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 9:49 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council
  at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of John R. Scola, to
  Monday, July 20, 2009 at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  13  July 6, 2009
 __________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 20, 2009

City Council Minutes  14  July 6, 2009
